`examples/Cpp/BrickPlay/AGENTS.md`:

```md
# AGENTS.md — BrickPlay Example

## Project context

This folder contains a small 3D toy called "BrickPlay" that lets users build worlds using building blocks referred to as "bricks" of various dimensions and colors.
They are placed in a 3D grid encoded via a kd-Tree representation to record occupied cells, perform ray-casting for user selection, and resolve camera collision detection.

## File Formats

BrickPlay uses two primary custom file formats for loading its configuration and loading/saving user generated worlds.
Both of these file formats follow a similar syntax as the Wavefront Object 3D file format.
They are parsed line-by-line whereas empty lines and lines starting with the hashtag character `#` are ignored as whitespaces/comments.
Statement lines begin with a single character specifying a command, followed by their parameters.

All numeric fields for bricks, grid, and bounding volume are in signed integers, only the camera setting uses floating-point numbers.
Filenames must not be wrapped in quotes and can therefore not contain whitespaces; They are parsed via the C++ stream `>>` operators.

### Configuration File Format

The configuration file *BrickPlay.config.txt* describes brick types, their identifier, dimensions,
where to load their 3D models (.obj format only) and into which group to load them,
and optionally which cells of their bounding box to ignore to allow shapes beyond basic 3D boxes (such as approximated/voxelated slope bricks).

These are the configuration file commands:
- `b ID W H D FILE [GROUP]` defines a brick named `ID` of dimension WxHxD and loads its .obj file into the specified group (or default group),
  e.g. `b 1x1x3  1 3 1  Bricks/Brick1x1x3.obj` loads "Brick1x1x3.obj" into the default group for a brick identified as "1x1x3".
  These identifiers are used in the following scene file format. `H` (height) and `D` (depth) might be swapped between the
  identifier/filename and their dimensional description.
  Multiple of these statements can be used for the same identifier to load multiple 3D models into various groups for the same brick ID.
  Valid groups are:
  - `Default` (or omitted) for the primary rendering of the model.
  - `WallsOnly` for an alternative model when the brick is blocked in the grid top and bottom.
  - `Transparent` for an alternative model that looks more appealing with transparent materials.
    This is not required for transparent bricks, but they are preferred.
- `e ID X Y Z` excludes the local cell at (X,Y,Z) from the brick specified by ID,
  e.g. `e 1x1x3 0 1 0` excludes the center cell of the 1x1x3 brick defined above.
- `v W H D` defines the bounding volume of the scene grid,
  e.g. `v 100 50 80` defines the grid size as 100 cells wide by 50 cells high by 100 cells deep.
  This defines the limits of all further grid coordaintes into the half-open ranges X `[-100/2, +100/2)`, Y `[0, +50)`, Z `[-80/2, +80/2)`.
- `p GRAYSCALE`/`p RGB`/`p RGBA` adds an entry to the color palette, either as gray-scaled value (e.g. `FF` for white),
  RGB value (e.g. `00FF00` for green), or RGBA value (e.g. `FFFF0080` for transparent yellow). They *must* be written as hex codes.
  They will appear as coloring options to the user but are independent of the color palettes defined in the scene file format.

### Scene File Format

User generated worlds are saved/loaded from the *Scenes/* subfolder.

These are the scene file commands:
- `c X Y Z PITCH YAW` defines the camera position at position (X,Y,Z) and with rotation PITCH (X-axis) and YAW (Y-axis) in degrees.
  This *should* appear exactly once as it overrides the previous camera setting.
- `p` command uses the same syntax as described above in the configuration file format section.
  The order in which these appear in the scene files determines how they are referenced in the following instancing command `i`.
  These commands describe color palette entries for the scene itself, while the one described in the previous section
  describe what users can select to paint their scene in the user interface.
  If more colors from the configuration are added or removed, the scene files will be unaffected.
- `b ID` makes the brick ID current, e.g. `b 1x1x3` causes all subsequent `i` commands to produce brick instances identified as "1x1x3" from the configuration file.
- `i X Y Z ROTATION COLOR` places a new brick instance into the scene at grid position (X,Y,Z).
  - `ROTATION` must be `0`, `90`, `180`, or `270` for their respective Y-axis rotation (in degrees).
  - `COLOR` defines the instance color and must be defined in one of the following patterns:
    - `p<INDEX>`, e.g. `p0` for the first color palette entry from the beginning of the scene file.
    - `GRAYSCALE`/`RGB`/`RGBA` just like the color palette values.
      These instances will receive the color with the closest 'distance' to the existing color palette from the configuration file;
      No new color can be described this way, but it prevents scenes from breaking entirely when the color palette changes.
- `o X Y Z` is an optional command not used by the scene writer that defines an offset to all subsequent instancing commands `i`.
  The offset (X,Y,Z) is added to the grid positions and allows users to quickly modify their scenes in a text editor.


```

`examples/Cpp/BrickPlay/BrickPlay.Brick.h`:

```h
/*
 * BrickPlay.Brick.h
 *
 * Copyright (c) 2015 Lukas Hermanns. All rights reserved.
 * Licensed under the terms of the BSD 3-Clause license (see LICENSE.txt).
 */

#ifndef LLGL_EXAMPLE_BRICKPLAY_BRICK_H
#define LLGL_EXAMPLE_BRICKPLAY_BRICK_H


#include <Gauss/Vector3.h>
#include <Gauss/Equals.h> // For Vector3 == operator
#include <GeometryUtils.h>
#include <LLGL/Utils/ForRange.h>
#include <string>
#include <cstdint>
#include <map>


#define INVALID_BRICK_ID UINT32_MAX

// 3D vector type for the Brick grid.
using GridVec3i = Gs::Vector3i;

// Axis-aligned bounding box for the Brick grid.
using AABB3i = AABB<GridVec3i>;


// How bricks can be rotated in this example. Only multiples of 90 degrees is supported.
enum GridRotation : std::uint8_t
{
    GridRotation_0 = 0,
    GridRotation_90,
    GridRotation_180,
    GridRotation_270,

    GridRotation_Num,
};

inline float ToDegrees(GridRotation gridRotation)
{
    return static_cast<float>(gridRotation * 90);
}

using BrickId = std::uint32_t;

enum BrickGroup : std::uint32_t
{
    BrickGroup_Default = 0, // Default opaque brick rendering
    BrickGroup_WallsOnly,   // Bricks rendered with an optimzied version, when blocked from above and below
    BrickGroup_Transparent, // Render bricks with different shaders
    BrickGroup_Invisible,   // Not rendered at all, for bricks that are blocked from all sides

    BrickGroup_Num,
};

// Brick vertex strucutre for brick instances. They are untextured, solid-colored bricks, so they don't need texture coordinates.
struct BrickVertex
{
    Gs::Vector3f position;
    Gs::Vector3f normal;
};

struct BrickMesh
{
    // Number of vertices to render.
    std::uint32_t numVertices = 0;

    // Zero-based index to the first vertex into the vertex buffer.
    std::uint32_t firstVertex = 0;
};

struct InstanceGroup
{
    // Debug label constructed from BrickId and BrickGroup. Pre-allocate to avoid string concatenation during rendering (minor optimization).
    std::string     debugName;

    // Number of instances to render for this group
    std::uint32_t   numInstances      = 0;

    // Zero-based index to the first instance into the global `instances` container for this group. Instance 0 is reserved for the preview instance.
    std::uint32_t   firstInstance     = 0;

    // Number of instances allocated for this group in the global `instances` container. This must always be greater than or equal to `numInstances`.
    std::uint32_t   instanceCapacity  = 0;
};

// Meta data for each brick.
struct BrickInfo
{
    std::string             label;
    GridVec3i               extent;
    std::vector<GridVec3i>  excludedCells;
    std::uint32_t           numGroups                       = 0;
    BrickMesh               meshes[BrickGroup_Num];
    InstanceGroup           instanceGroups[BrickGroup_Num];

    // Expands upper bound of how many groups are used for this brick type.
    void ExpandGroups(BrickGroup newGroup)
    {
        numGroups = std::max(numGroups, static_cast<std::uint32_t>(newGroup) + 1);
    }
};

struct BrickDimensions
{
    GridVec3i offset;
    GridVec3i extent;
};

inline std::uint32_t CombineToBrickId(int type, int group)
{
    return static_cast<std::uint32_t>(type * BrickGroup_Num + group);
}

inline BrickId GroupIdToBrickId(std::uint32_t groupId)
{
    return static_cast<BrickId>(groupId / BrickGroup_Num);
}

inline BrickGroup GroupIdToBrickGroup(std::uint32_t groupId)
{
    return static_cast<BrickGroup>(groupId % BrickGroup_Num);
}

// Helper class to convert BrickId to meta data and vice-versa.
class BrickDictionary
{

    std::vector<BrickVertex>        brickVertices;
    std::vector<BrickInfo>          brickInfos;
    std::map<std::string, BrickId>  labelToBrickId;

    BrickDictionary() = default;

public:

    BrickDictionary(const BrickDictionary&) = delete;
    BrickDictionary& operator = (const BrickDictionary&) = delete;

    // Returns this singleton instance.
    static BrickDictionary& Get()
    {
        static BrickDictionary self;
        return self;
    }

    // Returns the BrickInfo entry for the specified label.
    BrickInfo& FindOrInsert(std::string&& label)
    {
        auto it = labelToBrickId.find(label);
        if (it == labelToBrickId.end())
        {
            // Map label to brick ID
            labelToBrickId[label] = static_cast<BrickId>(brickInfos.size());

            // Add new entry
            brickInfos.push_back({});
            brickInfos.back().label = std::move(label);
            return brickInfos.back();
        }
        return brickInfos[it->second];
    }

    std::uint32_t NumBrickTypes() const
    {
        return static_cast<std::uint32_t>(brickInfos.size());
    }

    const BrickInfo& GetInfo(BrickId id) const
    {
        return brickInfos[id];
    }

    BrickInfo& GetInfo(BrickId id)
    {
        return brickInfos[id];
    }

    const BrickMesh& GetMesh(BrickId id, BrickGroup group = BrickGroup_Default) const
    {
        return GetInfo(id).meshes[group];
    }

    BrickMesh& GetMesh(BrickId id, BrickGroup group = BrickGroup_Default)
    {
        return GetInfo(id).meshes[group];
    }

    // Returns the specified BrickId as a string representation. Used by the scene file writer.
    const char* TypeToString(BrickId id) const
    {
        return (id < brickInfos.size() ? GetInfo(id).label.c_str() : "");
    }

    // Returns the BrickId that's mapped from the specified string. Used by the scene file reader.
    BrickId TypeFromString(const char* s) const
    {
        auto it = labelToBrickId.find(s);
        return (it != labelToBrickId.end() ? it->second : INVALID_BRICK_ID);
    }

    BrickId FindClosestTypeFromString(const char* s) const
    {
        for (const auto& it : labelToBrickId)
        {
            if (it.first.find(s) != std::string::npos)
                return it.second;
        }
        return INVALID_BRICK_ID;
    }

    BrickGroup GroupFromString(const char* s) const
    {
        if (::strcmp(s, "Default"    ) == 0) return BrickGroup_Default;
        if (::strcmp(s, "WallsOnly"  ) == 0) return BrickGroup_WallsOnly;
        if (::strcmp(s, "Transparent") == 0) return BrickGroup_Transparent;
        if (::strcmp(s, "Invisible"  ) == 0) return BrickGroup_Invisible;
        return BrickGroup_Num;
    }

    const char* GroupToString(BrickGroup g) const
    {
        switch (g)
        {
            case BrickGroup_Default :       return "Default";
            case BrickGroup_WallsOnly:      return "WallsOnly";
            case BrickGroup_Transparent:    return "Transparent";
            case BrickGroup_Invisible:      return "Invisible";
            default:                        return "";
        }
    }

    GridVec3i GetExtent(BrickId id) const
    {
        return (id < brickInfos.size() ? brickInfos[id].extent : GridVec3i{});
    }

    BrickDimensions GetBrickDimensions(BrickId id, GridRotation rotation) const
    {
        BrickDimensions brickDim;

        brickDim.extent = GetExtent(id);
        if (rotation == GridRotation_90 || rotation == GridRotation_270)
            std::swap(brickDim.extent.x, brickDim.extent.z);

        brickDim.offset.x = ((rotation == GridRotation_90 || rotation == GridRotation_180) ? -(brickDim.extent.x + 1)/2 : -brickDim.extent.x/2);
        brickDim.offset.y = 0;
        brickDim.offset.z = ((rotation == GridRotation_180 || rotation == GridRotation_270) ? -(brickDim.extent.z + 1)/2 : -brickDim.extent.z/2);

        return brickDim;
    }

    BrickId FindBrickIdForDimension(const GridVec3i& extent) const
    {
        // Try to find brick with the specified dimensions
        for (BrickId id = 0; id < brickInfos.size(); ++id)
        {
            if (brickInfos[id].extent == extent)
                return id;
        }
        return INVALID_BRICK_ID; // No such brick found
    }

    // Imports the specified vertices and assigned them to the output mesh.
    void ImportMesh(BrickMesh& outMesh, const std::vector<TexturedVertex>& inVertices)
    {
        outMesh.firstVertex = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(brickVertices.size());
        outMesh.numVertices = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(inVertices.size());

        brickVertices.resize(brickVertices.size() + inVertices.size());

        auto ConvertVertex = [](BrickVertex& dst, const TexturedVertex& src) -> void
        {
            dst.position    = src.position;
            dst.normal      = src.normal;
        };

        for_range(i, outMesh.numVertices)
            ConvertVertex(brickVertices[outMesh.firstVertex + i], inVertices[i]);
    }

    // Returns the entire container of all brick vertices.
    const std::vector<BrickVertex>& GetBrickVertices() const
    {
        return brickVertices;
    }

};

// Returns true if the specified brick ID has a mesh that only renders its walls.
inline bool IsBrickTypeOptimized(BrickId id)
{
    return (BrickDictionary::Get().GetInfo(id).meshes[BrickGroup_WallsOnly].numVertices > 0);
}

// Brick handle to reference an instance in the grid.
// These change as bricks are being transferred between groups for optimized rendering.
// It's important to keep this in mind especially inside 
struct Brick
{
    static constexpr std::uint32_t groupIdBits      = 8;
    static constexpr std::uint32_t groupIdInvalid   = (1u << groupIdBits) - 1;

    /*static_assert(
        (1u << groupIdBits) > BrickType_Num * BrickGroup_Num,
        "Not enough bits to encode `BrickType x BrickGroup` elements; Increase `Brick::groupIdBits` when adding elements to BrickType or BrickGroup!"
    );*/

    Brick() :
        groupId       { groupIdInvalid },
        groupInstance { 0              }
    {
    }

    Brick(std::uint32_t groupId, std::uint32_t groupInstance) :
        groupId       { groupId       },
        groupInstance { groupInstance }
    {
    }

    // Combined brick type and group.
    std::uint32_t   groupId         : groupIdBits;

    // Index into the group's instance. Use `group.firstInstance + groupInstance` to get index into global `instances` container.
    std::uint32_t   groupInstance   : (32 - groupIdBits);

    void SetId(BrickId id)
    {
        groupId = id * BrickGroup_Num + GroupIdToBrickGroup(groupId);
    }

    BrickId GetId() const
    {
        return GroupIdToBrickId(groupId);
    }

    void SetGroup(BrickGroup group)
    {
        groupId = GroupIdToBrickId(groupId) * BrickGroup_Num + group;
    }

    BrickGroup GetGroup() const
    {
        return GroupIdToBrickGroup(groupId);
    }

    operator bool() const
    {
        return (groupId != groupIdInvalid);
    }

    bool operator == (const Brick& rhs) const
    {
        return (groupId == rhs.groupId && groupInstance == rhs.groupInstance);
    }

    bool operator != (const Brick& rhs) const
    {
        return !(*this == rhs);
    }

    // Required for std::set. Without it, the implicit bool conversion would be used and treat all valid bricks as equal.
    bool operator < (const Brick& rhs) const
    {
        if (groupId != rhs.groupId)
            return (groupId < rhs.groupId);
        else
            return (groupInstance < rhs.groupInstance);
    }
};


#endif // /LLGL_EXAMPLE_BRICKPLAY_BRICK_H
```

```h
    static constexpr float          cameraCollisionRadius           = 1.5f;

    static constexpr float          previewBlockOffsetY             = 0.075f;   // Y-axis world position offset for the preview block before putting it into place

    static constexpr float          silhouetteColor[3]              = { 1.0f, 1.0f, 0.0f }; // Color of the silhouette outline for selectin bricks
    static constexpr float          silhouetteWidth                 = 5.0f;

    static constexpr float          uiMenuTriggerDistCoeff          = 1.0f;     // Percentage to menu bar width of how many pixels the user has to drag the menu bar until it starts scrolling or pulling out bricks

    static constexpr int            outputThumbnailSamples          = 8;        // Number of samples to render the thumbnails with when writing them out to PNG file

    static const LLGL::ColorRGBAub  uiSideMenuColor;
    static constexpr GridRotation   uiThumbnailDefaultRotation      = GridRotation_270;
    static constexpr float          uiThumbnailMinVolumeSize        = 3.0f;     // Minimum size for a bounding volume of brick thumbnails.

    static constexpr std::uint8_t   uiThumbstickBgOpacity           = 180;
    static constexpr int            uiThumbstickDeadZone            = 5;        // How many pixels thumbsticks have to move before they are triggered

    static constexpr int            maxBrickExtent                  = 16;       // Limit how large bricks can be in X/Y/Z dimension

    static constexpr int            planeSubdivisions               = 1;

    static constexpr int            heightFieldChunkSize            = 2;        // Build bricks from height field in 4x4 grid chunks so that the largest bricks can be utilized

    static constexpr std::size_t    maxHistoryLength                = 50;       // Maxmimum number of steps to undo

    static constexpr int            numAddedBricksUntilSharing      = 20;       // Users need to add at least this many bricks before they can share their creation

    static constexpr float          animTimeToLiftUp                = 0.1f;     // Time (in seconds) for the preview brick to lift up. This should feel almost instantaneous.
    static constexpr float          animDelayBeforeSettleDown       = 0.15f;    // Time (in seconds) before the animation for the preview brick to settle down begins.
    static constexpr float          animTimeToSettleDown            = 0.1f;     // Time (in seconds) for the preview brick to settle down.
    static constexpr float          animLiftYAxis                   = 0.3f;     // Units to lift up the preview brick (Y-axis).

    // The preview brick motion is a stiff damped spring integrated with semi-implicit Euler, which is only stable for small time steps.
    // Larger frame times are split into substeps of at most this duration (in seconds). Since 60 FPS frames never need to be split, their behavior is unchanged.
    static constexpr float          animMaxTimeStep                 = 1.0f/50.0f;
    static constexpr int            animMaxSubsteps                 = 16;       // Upper bound of substeps per frame. Beyond this, the animation slows down instead of becoming unstable.

    // Logarithm slows higher motion down quickly, but is still open ended. So this constant is just a target upper value, not a hard limit.
    static constexpr float          animMotionTargetAngle           = 8.0f;

    // Whether to use extended brick models for their optimized versions (*_WallsOnlyExt.obj).
    // If false, covered bricks can show tiny holes due to beveled edges of bricks sitting above and below them.
    // This can be turned off for mobile platforms where this flaw is virtually invisible
    // and the incurred performance cost of more almost invisible geometry can be avoided.
    static constexpr bool           useWaterTightBrickOptimization  = true;
}; // /namespace Cfg

const LLGL::ColorRGBAub  Cfg::uiBrickThumbnailBgColor = { 180, 180, 180, 255 };
const LLGL::ColorRGBAub  Cfg::uiSideMenuColor         = { 0, 0, 0, 180 };


#endif // /LLGL_EXAMPLE_BRICKPLAY_UTILS_H
```
